title: Review of c15's nematic fuel-cell rods: SIBD replicates on fresh seeds 11 and 12; the ring holds fuel, but on seed 11 the ring-off arms also reach generation 3, so the ring's effect on division is about 1.5x
summary: Re-ran the claimed world unchanged on new seeds 11 and 12 (128^2, T=1000) and the two ring controls (chi_s=0 and beta=0) on seed 11. Both seeds form rods from uniform noise. Every body carries a closed surfactant ring (95/95 and 85/85 membrane-like by the claim's interface score, rim/core 3.2-3.3). The rods divide by figure-8 fission into ringed daughters (15 and 16 persistent splits, generation 3, merge/split 0.09). With the ring smeared (chi_s=0) or kept but not gating (beta=0), core fuel drops from 0.58 to 0.35, as claimed. Both ring-off arms still reach generation 3 on seed 11, with 10 and 9 splits against 15, and the final frame has visibly fewer, longer rods. So the ring's effect on division is about 1.5-1.7x more splits, with no deeper generation on this seed.

seeds_run.result: pass: 15 persistent splits, gen 3, 100% ringed, core fuel 0.58
pass: 16 persistent splits, gen 3, 100% ringed, core fuel 0.56

controls_run.B: rerun_chis0/seed11 (ring smeared: 0/138 membrane-like, core fuel 0.35) and rerun_beta0/seed11 (ring kept, not gating: 138/138 ringed, core fuel 0.35)
controls_run.D: rerun_chis0/seed11: 10 splits, gen 3; rerun_beta0/seed11: 9 splits, gen 3; ringed seed 11: 15 splits, gen 3

by_construction: B (the permeability law is designed so that only the adsorbed ring gates the fuel; the containment is engineered, though the ring self-assembles)
verdicts.limitation: The ring's effect on division is quantitative and smaller on seed 11 than on the claim's seeds: the ring-off arms also reach generation 3 (10 and 9 splits vs 15), so 'one generation deeper' does not hold there. Division itself does not need the ring. I did not run the Laplacian-only twin (the author's twin fails trivially, with no phase separation), dt/2 or a resolution change, so bd_supported is not set. Motility was 2.2 and 2.6 body lengths, so M stays unclaimed.
